transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-05
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Priya Nair (Redwood AE), Ben Carter (Redwood SE), Mike Reynolds (Valence - CPO), Sonia Patel (Valence - Legal), Dr. Karen Liu (Valence - Head of AI), Jorge Martinez (Valence - Procurement)

Summary:
Quick procurement review focused on finalizing MSA/DPA, confirming SLAs, pricing approval path, and next steps for vendor onboarding. Action owners and dates agreed at end.

Topics:
- MSA redlines and DPA specifics (data residency, retention, breach notifications)
- SLAs (uptime, latency SLOs for hosted vs dedicated)
- Security artifacts (SOC2, ISO, KMS/HSM, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs)
- Pricing approval process and pilot commitments
- Vendor onboarding and timelines

Transcript:
[00:00] Priya: hey everyone, thanks for joining on time, really appreciate it. i'm priya from redwood inference, and with me is ben carter our solutions engineer.
[00:18] Ben: hi all, yeah happy to be here. will go through the technical bits later but first want to make sure legal/procurement items are clear.
[00:32] Mike: thanks priya, we've got about 45-60 minutes, goal is to get to a point where procurement and legal know next steps.
[00:45] Sonia: hi, i'm sonia from legal, i'll be focused on the MSA and DPA. we also have some security questionnaire items to close.
[00:54] Jorge: procurement here, need to understand approval path for pricing and vendor onboarding timeline.
[01:02] Priya: perfect. quick agenda: 1) MSA/DPA redlines 2) SLAs and service model differences (hosted vs dedicated) 3) security docs 4) pricing approvals and pilot 5) next steps. sound good?
[01:18] Sonia: yes.
[01:22] Ben: yep.
[01:26] Priya: ok first on MSA, we've circulated a standard redwood MSA and a separate DPA. can you tell us what redlines you expect?
[01:38] Sonia: there are a few things. on DPA: data residency for EMEA patient data — we need a clause that ensures storage and processing within EEA unless we agree otherwise. also retention limits, and stronger breach notification timings.
[01:56] Priya: understood. our platform supports region pinning for hosted customers and we have private deployment options for full on-prem; we can commit to EEA residency for a Dedicated or Private deployment, and for hosted we can use EU regions. about breach notification, our standard is 72 hours, is that ok or do you need shorter?
[02:15] Sonia: 48 hours would be preferable for high-risk patient data, but we can take 72 if there's escalations built in and SLO on remediation.
[02:26] Priya: good note. we'll flag that with legal but priya: (transcription glitch) — sorry, we'll flag that for escalation in the MSA redline.
[02:36] Mike: on retention — we want a maximum of 30 days for logs and no retention of PII in model fine-tuning data. can you confirm?
[02:47] Ben: yes, valence. by default we don't persist user data for training in hosted; we have explicit options, and the DPA can state no training unless agreed. logs retention is configurable and we can set 30 days for this engagement.
[03:02] Dr. Karen: technical q: how do you do key management? we need customer-managed keys / HSM for encryption at rest.
[03:13] Ben: we support KMS integrations and customer-managed keys on Dedicated and Private deployments; for hosted we offer KMS envelope encryption with customer KMS options depending on region — sometimes we can do BYOK for high tiers. not all regions support BYOK today but we can scope it.
[03:30] [crosstalk] Jorge: sorry, BYOK?
[03:33] Priya: bring your own key.
[03:35] Jorge: thanks.
[03:38] Sonia: related to that, can you provide SOC 2 Type II and latest penetration test?
[03:45] Priya: yes, we have SOC 2 Type II and a security whitepaper, plus pen test summary available under an NDA. we'll attach those to the DPA package.
[03:58] Mike: what about SLAs? we care about latency SLOs as well as uptime — especially for real-time clinical workflows.
[04:08] Ben: for hosted API our standard SLA is 99.9% availability, and latency SLO depends on model and sequence length; typical p95 is quoted in the performance profile. for predictable low-latency we recommend Dedicated or Private which have tighter latency distributions.
[04:28] Mike: do you commit to a latency number in the MSA for dedicated? procurement may want a hard SLO.
[04:36] Priya: we can include a service level addendum for Dedicated with the expected p95 for the committed capacity. exact numbers depend on model/sequence, but we can include an example or a performance appendix and tie credits to missed SLOs.
[04:54] Sonia: what is the penalty or credit structure? finance will want clarity.
[04:59] Priya: typical approach is service credits scaled by minutes of downtime or percentage breach; we can propose a tiered credit schedule for dedicated capacity. i'll include the template.
[05:12] Dr. Karen: also want to check about fallback behavior — if a model variant is unavailable do you have automated fallback to a smaller model?
[05:20] Ben: yes, smart routing and fallbacks are part of the platform — we can configure failover to a compatible model family. tradeoffs: lower quality vs availability.
[05:34] Mike: procurement question: pricing approvals — we have a pilot budget and then a larger commit for Dedicated if pilot meets SLAs. what approval path do you recommend?
[05:44] Priya: typical flow: pilot (self-serve or short-term reserved) -> internal eval -> procurement/finance approves committed capacity (monthly/annual). we can supply a pricing sheet + example TCO comparisons (hosted vs dedicated vs private).
[05:58] Jorge: who signs the MSA and how long does vendor onboarding take?
[06:04] Priya: MSA is signed by an authorized Redwood officer; onboarding time varies: hosted pilot can start within 1-2 weeks after SOW, Dedicated provisioning is usually 4-8 weeks depending on capacity and regions, Private on-prem similar to Dedicated plus extra lead time for network.
[06:22] Jorge: procurement needs exact timelines for finance approval. can you provide a timeline document?
[06:27] Priya: yes we'll send a proposed timeline with milestones.
[06:31] Sonia: there's also the vendor risk assessment — we use a vendor security questionnaire that requires fairly detailed answers and attachments.
[06:39] Ben: we've got a completed vendor questionnaire template plus SOC2 docs we can share. some customers prefer to run an on-site/zoom pen test, but usually the docs and attestation suffice.
[06:54] Sonia: do you offer SSO/SAML and SCIM for provisioning? we need SAML-based SSO and RBAC integration for user management.
[07:03] Ben: yes SSO via SAML is supported, SCIM for provisioning, and RBAC roles are customizable. for hosted we manage the auth layer; for Dedicated/Private you can integrate with your IdP directly.
[07:17] Mike: are audit logs available for admin actions and request-level logs? we need to show access logs for compliance.
[07:25] Ben: yes, audit logs are available and can be exported to your SIEM; request-level logs are configurable and we can limit retention to meet your policies.
[07:35] Sonia: liability cap in MSA — we may need to negotiate higher cap for PHI-related workloads.
[07:42] Priya: typical MSA has a liability cap tied to fees paid, but enterprise customers can request higher caps in exchange for pricing or insurance terms; we'll note that as a negotiation point.
[07:56] [small pause]
[08:02] Jorge: on pricing, can you give an example price for a short pilot — say 100k tokens per day for 30 days, and then an annual committed Dedicated price for the equivalent throughput?
[08:12] Priya: i'll include a pricing sheet with a pilot estimate and committed reserved pricing. rough order: hosted pay-as-you-go for X tokens, Dedicated monthly commit depends on GPU type and utilization; we'll prepare an apples-to-apples TCO.
[08:26] Mike: we need procurement to see the pricing sheet before we can approve pilot spend.
[08:31] Priya: understood — i'll send pricing with a line-item breakdown and sample invoices.
[08:36] Sonia: what about data residency proof? we need a clause and an appendix showing region control.
[08:42] Ben: we can provide region control statements and a diagram of how requests are routed. for Dedicated/Private it's more direct and we can provide SLA-backed region guarantees.
[08:55] Dr. Karen: technical note — for the pilot we want to run a small latency benchmark using our sample prompts and obfuscated PHI. ben, can you run that?
[09:03] Ben: yes, happy to run a benchmark against hosted EU region or a temporary Dedicated slice if you want — we'll need sample prompt set and the data keys; we'll obfuscate PHI in the test.
[09:16] Mike: timeline — if we get the pricing and MSA this week, legal will review next week; procurement wants onboarding completed by mid-November if possible.
[09:26] Priya: we'll prioritize documents this week.
[09:30] Sonia: one more question: do you support a hold harmless for downstream clinical outcomes?
[09:36] Priya: we typically disclaim downstream liability and encourage customers to own application-level clinical decisions; we can discuss tighter terms but it's usually a negotiation point.
[09:48] Sonia: ok noted.
[09:51] Jorge: any competitors you think we should be aware of on the SLA/pricing side?
[09:56] Priya: common alternatives mentioned were Anthropic and OpenAI's managed offerings, also AWS Bedrock for some large customers; we'll include a short competitive note.
[10:07] Ben: technical caveat — different providers have different latency/cost tradeoffs and different data handling terms, so it's worth looking at the TCO.
[10:17] Mike: let's get to next steps.
[10:19] Priya: recap of actions: priya to send redlined MSA and DPA and SOC2 + pen test summary under NDA; ben to run latency benchmark with your prompt set; sonia to return redlines; jorge to start onboarding form. dates we suggested in the doc.
[10:34] Sonia: yes that matches internal expectations.
[10:38] Jorge: procurement will need a short vendor pack for finance.
[10:42] Priya: we'll attach a vendor pack with invoices, pricing, and timeline.
[10:46] Mike: if we get everything in the next 7-10 days we can start a pilot mid-November.
[10:52] Priya: great — we'll aim for that.
[10:55] Ben: i'll ask for the sample prompt set and a point of contact for the benchmark.
[10:59] Dr. Karen: i'll send obfuscated prompts and sample size by end of day tomorrow.
[11:05] Priya: perfect. any other questions?
[11:08] Sonia: none from legal, thanks.
[11:10] Jorge: none.
[11:12] Priya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the doc bundle and next steps. meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: automatic transcription had some mis-hears e.g., "BYOK" spelled out, occasional speaker attribution inconsistencies.
